newsitem.title: UK: Copper, aluminium, zinc shine by LME close.
newsitem.headline: Copper, aluminium, zinc shine by LME close.

text.p: A robust trio of metals ended LME ring trading on Thursday with strong gains after gingerly testing higher levels.
Zinc climbed to fresh two-year peaks, copper came within a whisker of regaining the $2,300 mark and aluminium wrapped up the day by wiping out more corrective losses.
Three months copper closed the afternoon kerb at $2,275 per tonne, up $25, but well off the morning high of $2,295.
"It had a good run in the morning, so it wasn't surprising to see some profit-taking," a trader said.
Nearby tightness was keeping the market on the boil ahead of Third Wednesday pricing next week, with some shorts waiting until the last minute to cover, analysts said.
Belated borrowing against the previous day's prompt (tom/next) traded at the LME limit of $24 in the morning but the premium of cash over three months material eased by about $20 to $95/$100.
Floor traders earlier said stocks data on Friday was expected to be level to 3,000 tonnes higher, but another trader said later inventories may rise by as much as 7,000 tonnes.

Zinc gained $35 or three percent on the day to end at $1,221 after fund buying propelled it above $1,200 in the morning, which in turn triggered stops and fuelled more speculative and technical buying.
It ran into strong selling at its high of $1,228, traders said.
The market was heading towards a technical target of $1,239, the high from January 1995 and moving back into overbought territory, chartists said.
Aluminium got a boost from Chinese buying in the afternoon, sending it to a peak of $1,578. The market ended just $2 off the high, a gain on the day of $21.
The market has rebounded strongly since bottoming on Tuesday at $1,534 in what analysts called a correction to its four-month uptrend.
Nickel finished the day unchanged at $7,880 after touching $7,940 in the morning.
Lead added $7 to $656 and tin gained $5 to $5,940.
Alloy was indicated higher at $1,490/92 after Wednesday's close of $1,466.
